turns.input: *He asks Livia Marr who they think he is and where he comes from.*
turns.narration:
In Heartstone Square, with the tower's heavy wooden entrance looming behind him and the disreputable Coined Lie tavern visible somewhere in the low buildings nearby, Nicco turns his question to the small, narrow-framed woman with dark-blond hair pinned up and a measuring tape around her neck. Livia Marr regards him with quick, assessing eyes, three pins held casually between her lips as she looks him up and down.

She removes the pins to speak, blunt and energetic. "Who you are? A man standing in square mid-morning asking strange questions of a tailor he's never met." She runs the tape measure through her fingers without looking at it, still studying his face. "Where from? Your clothes say nothing useful—decent fabric, wrong cut for anywhere I know. Could be custom, could be foreign, could be you dressed in the dark." A quick, not unkind smile. "You want me to guess? I don't guess. Guessing wrong hurts my pride, and I have enough of that."

She tilts her head, measuring tape still moving through her hands. "Why ask me? I sew for West District families and mend what they bring. Your business is your own unless you make it mine."

[CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE ACCESS]
Facts: F1 campaign_fact_nicco_light_mage "Nicco is a Light mage." | F2 campaign_fact_nicco_otherworlder "Nicco came to this world from another world." | H1 household "Nicco is owner of the household Heartstone."
Narration and Nicco (player): F1, F2, H1. Nicco's speech and decisions still belong to the player.
Livia Marr: CAN USE none; DO NOT USE F1, F2, H1
A character may voice or act on only the facts listed CAN USE for them (believes/suspects/heard_rumor: only as belief, suspicion or rumor). DO NOT USE also covers hints, rumors, "everyone says" talk and claims that imply the fact; do not invent rumors or public talk to get around it. DO NOT USE is this turn's permission, not proof of ignorance: that character may ask, say they have not heard, or defer to someone who can use it.
UNKNOWN IS NOT A RUMOR: when a character cannot use a fact, it is unknown to them, never something they heard. "People say", "I heard", "word is", "everyone knows", registries, records, reports, past meetings or sightings are sources; a character may cite one only when a CAN USE entry with that basis exists. Allowed instead: "I don't know", a question, or a guess explicitly framed as a guess and based only on what they can see or hear right now.
